minutes.headline: Select Board ratified new DPW director and conservation administrator, and conditionally approved four student geocaches.
minutes.summary: The Select Board met after annual town meeting and reviewed how it went, including the defeat of the 30 School Street design funding and plans to bring it back at a special town meeting. It ratified two town manager appointments, approved a toll booth fundraiser and a senior project, and heard the town manager's report and FY22 goals update. ARPA spending was discussed without a plan, and routine warrants and a water commitment were handled.

public_comment.topic: Resident praised the town meeting format and citizen input; raised concerns about off-the-cuff floor amendments, urged vetting of capital project lists and opposed item-by-item capital votes, and discussed the electronic clickers and quorum.

votes.motion: Approve the Boys and Girls Club toll booth fundraiser on May 21, 9 a.m. to 1 p.m., rain date June 11.
Ratify the town manager's appointment of William Bernard as DPW director.
Approve the town manager's appointment of Nadia Madden as conservation administrator.
Approve John McCormack's request to install four geocaches on town property, contingent on approval by DPW and the chief of police.
Approve the fourth quarter water commitment.

budget_items.what_was_said: Town expects to hear in summer on EPA brownfields assessment funding under the federal infrastructure bill for tank removal and limited soil removal. Tax title foreclosure is being started.
Federal community project funding request did not make the appropriations committee. A small bridge grant application is pending with MassDOT, with word expected in June.
A shelter operator may seek ARPA funds from the town; no proposal had been received. Funds must be committed by end of 2024 and expended by 2026.
The board approved the fourth quarter water commitment for the town water department.

what_happened.line: The Select Board ratified the town manager's appointments of a new DPW director and a new conservation administrator, both unanimously.

The board reviewed annual town meeting, where an amendment to cut funding and drop design work at 30 School Street passed narrowly; the board leans toward a standalone article at a special town meeting.
The board approved four student geocaches on town property, contingent on approval by the DPW and the chief of police.
The board approved the fourth quarter water commitment and a Boys and Girls Club toll booth fundraiser.
ARPA spending was discussed with no proposal in hand; a shelter operator may ask for funds, which must be committed by the end of 2024.

why_it_matters: The 30 School Street design funding may come back to voters at a special town meeting, so residents may be asked to vote on it a second time.
ARPA money is still unallocated and has committed-by and spent-by deadlines, so how it is used is a decision still ahead for the town.
watch_next: A special town meeting warrant that may carry a standalone 30 School Street design funding article.
A further meeting on the means-tested senior property tax exemption, to be scheduled as soon as possible.
